initialization_sequence: 1. Power-up: Host ramps Vcc and VccQ (per Section 2.14 staggered if multiple targets share rail).
2. Host de-asserts CE_n (HIGH) initially; WP_n LOW for write protection during boot.
3. Host waits for power stable (Vcc/VccQ within operating range).
4. Host asserts CE_n LOW; issues Reset (FFh).
5. Device drives R/B_n LOW; host waits for R/B_n HIGH (up to 5 ms for first reset; max 500 µs for subsequent resets).
6. Host issues Read ID (90h) with address 20h. Device returns 'ONFI' signature (4Fh, 4Eh, 46h, 49h). Confirms ONFI compliance.
7. Host issues Read ID (90h) with address 00h. Device returns ≥ 4 ID bytes (Manufacturer ID, Device ID, vendor-defined).

8. Host issues Read Parameter Page (ECh + 00h). Device returns 256-byte Parameter Page + redundant copies. Host validates Integrity CRC (polynomial 8005h, init 4F4Eh); on mismatch reads the next redundant copy.
9. (Optional) Host issues Read Unique ID (EDh + 00h). Device returns 16 × (UID + complement). Host iterates copies until UID XOR complement = all ones.
10. Host parses Parameter Page geometry: bytes_per_page, spare_per_page, pages_per_block, blocks_per_LUN, LUNs_per_target, address_cycle_counts, plane_address_bits, ECC requirements.
11. Host parses Parameter Page timing-mode bitmaps (SDR bytes 129-130; NV-DDR bytes 144-145; NV-DDR2 bytes 142-143 + 162; NV-DDR3 bytes 160-161).
12. Host scans factory defect map: for each block, reads first or last page spare area; non-FFh = bad block; builds bad-block table.
13. (Optional NV-DDR / NV-DDR2 / NV-DDR3) Host issues Set Features (EFh + 01h Timing Mode) with P1 = data interface + mode; device switches data interface after tFEAT.
14. (NV-DDR2 / NV-DDR3) Host issues Set Features (EFh + 02h NV-DDR2/3 Configuration) to enable differential DQS / RE, ODT, warmup cycles.
15. (NV-DDR2 / NV-DDR3) Host issues ZQ Calibration Long (F9h). Device drives R/B_n LOW for tZQCL.
16. (NV-DDR3) Host runs Implicit DCC Training (18h), Read DQ Training (62h), Write TX DQ Training (63h pattern + 64h readback), Write RX DQ Training (76h).
17. (CE_n reduction) Host runs Volume Appointment via ENi/ENo enumeration; programs Volume Address via Set Features (58h); uses Volume Select (E1h) to direct subsequent commands.
18. Host de-asserts WP_n (HIGH) for Program/Erase enablement.
19. Device is now ready for application Read / Program / Erase operations.
page_read_sequence: 2. Host issues 5 address cycles (2 column + 3 row): C1, C2, R1, R2, R3.
4. After tWB, device drives R/B_n LOW; performs array→page-register read for tR.
5. Device drives R/B_n HIGH; host polls Read Status (70h) or Read Status Enhanced (78h).
6. (EZ NAND) Host checks FAIL bit before reading; if FAIL=1, no data transfer.
7. Host issues 00h again (Read Definition: re-issuing 00h causes device to start streaming from the selected column).
8. Host pulses RE_n (SDR) or DQS edges (NV-DDR family) to clock out bytes from the page register.
9. Host may use Change Read Column (05h + 2 col + E0h) + tCCS to reposition within the page register.
page_program_sequence: 2. Host issues 5 address cycles: C1, C2, R1, R2, R3.
3. Host streams write data bytes via WE_n cycles (SDR) or DQS edges (NV-DDR family); after the second address byte host shall wait tADL before the first data cycle.
4. (Optional) Host may interleave Change Write Column (85h + 2 col) to reposition within the page register; tCCS applies.
6. After tWB, device drives R/B_n LOW; performs page-register→array program for tPROG.
7. Device drives R/B_n HIGH; host polls Read Status (70h); checks FAIL bit.
block_erase_sequence: 2. Host issues 3 row address cycles: R1, R2, R3 (column ignored).
4. After tWB, device drives R/B_n LOW for tBERS.
5. Device drives R/B_n HIGH; host polls Read Status (70h); checks FAIL bit.
6. Erase of factory-marked bad block shall fail (FAIL bit set).
multi_plane_program_sequence: 1. Host issues 80h + plane0 address + plane0 data + 11h (commit plane 0 to multi-plane queue).
2. Host issues 80h + plane1 address + plane1 data + 10h (commit plane 1 and trigger concurrent program).
3. After tWB, device drives R/B_n LOW for tPROG (multi-plane).
4. Host polls Read Status Enhanced (78h) per plane for per-plane FAIL bit.
multi_plane_erase_sequence: 1. Host issues 60h + plane0 row addr + D1h.
2. Host issues 60h + plane1 row addr + D0h.
3. After tWB, device drives R/B_n LOW for tBERS (multi-plane).
4. Host polls Read Status Enhanced (78h) per plane for per-plane FAIL bit.
multi_plane_read_sequence: 3. Device performs concurrent reads; R/B_n LOW for tR.
4. Device drives R/B_n HIGH; host issues Read Status Enhanced per plane + Change Read Column Enhanced (06h + 5 addr + E0h) to select page-register output.
page_cache_program_sequence: 1. Host issues 80h + addr + data + 15h (commit page 0 to cache; device starts programming).
2. Host issues 80h + addr + data + 15h (commit page 1 to cache; device continues page 0 program, queues page 1).
3. Host polls Read Status; bit 6 RDY=1 means cache ready for next page; bit 5 ARDY=1 means array idle; bit 1 FAILC reports prior page result.
4. Host issues final 80h + addr + data + 10h (commit last page; non-cache).
5. Device drives R/B_n LOW for tPROG (last page); ARDY indicates array idle when complete.
read_cache_sequence: 1. Host issues 00h + addr + 31h (Read Cache Random; loads page 0 into cache).
2. Host polls Read Status; RDY=1 when cache ready.
3. Host pulses RE_n (or DQS edges) to read page 0; host issues 31h (Read Cache Sequential) to advance to next sequential page.
4. Host issues 3Fh (Read Cache End) to terminate; device drives R/B_n HIGH after last page transferred.
copyback_sequence: 1. Host issues 00h + source_addr + 35h (Copyback Read); device loads source page into page register; R/B_n LOW for tR.
2. (Optional) Host may modify a subset of bytes via Change Write Column / Small Data Move (85h + col + data).
3. Host issues 85h + destination_addr + 10h (Copyback Program); R/B_n LOW for tPROG; checks FAIL bit.
4. Used for wear-leveling moves without host data path (intra-LUN, intra-plane).
zq_calibration_sequence: 1. After Reset: host issues F9h (ZQ Calibration Long); R/B_n LOW for tZQCL (≥ 1 µs).
2. Periodic: host issues D9h (ZQ Calibration Short) per device-reported interval; R/B_n LOW for tZQCS.
3. Device updates output driver impedance against external RZQ (300 Ω ±1 % typ).
4. Host checks FAIL bit; FAIL=1 indicates calibration failure (driver impedance not within target).
data_interface_switch_sequence: 1. Host completes any pending operation; ARDY = 1.
2. Host issues Set Features (EFh + 01h Timing Mode) with P1 = target data interface + mode.
3. Device drives R/B_n LOW for tFEAT.
4. Device drives R/B_n HIGH; bus is now in the new data interface.
5. (If switching to NV-DDR2 / NV-DDR3) Host issues Set Features (EFh + 02h NV-DDR2/3 Configuration) + ZQ Calibration Long + (NV-DDR3) training.
ce_n_pin_reduction_enumeration_sequence: 1. Power-up; first target ENi tied LOW by board; subsequent targets ENi connected to previous ENo.
2. Host asserts CE_n LOW (single shared pin); issues Reset (FFh) — all targets reset.
3. Host issues Set Features (EFh + 58h Volume Configuration) with chosen Volume Address; ONLY the first target (ENi LOW) accepts; others ignore.
4. After tFEAT, first target asserts ENo HIGH; next target now sees ENi HIGH and is ready to accept its Volume Address.
5. Host repeats Set Features (58h) with next Volume Address; iterate until all targets enumerated.
6. Subsequent commands prefixed by Volume Select (E1h + Volume Address) direct to a specific target.
hot_removal_recovery: 1. ONFI does not specify hot-insert / hot-remove of soldered NAND packages; consumer-removable form factors (microSD, USB drive) sit at a higher layer.
2. On unexpected reset / glitch, host issues Reset (FFh); validates Parameter Page CRC; rebuilds bad-block table if necessary.
